findings.title: Opaque hashes hide the asserted schema contract
findings.why_it_matters: A legitimate tool-schema change produces only a digest mismatch, so the expected properties, required fields, enums, and defaults cannot be reviewed from this test. Updating the gate becomes a copy-the-new-hash workflow, which makes it easy to bless an unintended schema change while preserving a green but semantically opaque test.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the normalization step, but compare the normalized schemas with readable checked-in JSON fixtures or Jest snapshots so failures show the exact structural change; derive the expected tool-name ordering from that same fixture.
evidence: Lines 43-68 encode all 24 expected schemas only as SHA-256 strings rather than reviewable schema structures.
Lines 416-423 compare only name/digest pairs, so Jest can report which tool changed and the new hash, but not which schema keyword changed.
Lines 13-38 and 43-68 maintain tool identity in two parallel fixtures, with line 415 adding an assertion solely to keep those duplicate sources synchronized.

findings.title: Independent gates are coupled into one long scenario
findings.why_it_matters: The 150-line test stops at the first assertion failure, so an initialization or inventory mismatch prevents the persistence and semantic-export gates from running. This masks simultaneous regressions and makes future maintainers rerun or temporarily edit one broad test instead of selecting the failing contract area directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a small server/session fixture that owns startup, initialization, teardown, and temporary storage, then split tool-advertisement assertions from the create/connect/persist/export workflow while keeping the latter as one end-to-end scenario.
evidence: The single test beginning at line 363 covers initialize metadata (lines 374-394), tool inventory and schemas (401-424), tool behavior (426-463), semantic XML export (465-505), and disk persistence (507-510).
Jest aborts the test body on the first failed expectation; the finally block cleans up but no later gate in this scenario executes.
The protocol-advertisement checks do not depend on the BPMN process created later, so their coupling is test-structure rather than domain-flow complexity.

residual_risks: The custom stdio request helper is intentionally sequential; concurrent requests would attach competing stdout listeners and are not supported by its current shape.
testing_gaps: The lifecycle table proves startup-timeout cleanup, but no targeted case forces a post-start response timeout and verifies that the enclosing cleanup path leaves no child process.
